questions.prompt: What is Big-O notation, and why is it important in technical interviews? Answer in 2–4 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains Big-O describes the growth rate or upper bound of time or memory as input size increases
Mentions worst-case analysis or dropping constant multipliers and smaller terms
Explains interviewers use it to evaluate if code scales efficiently to large datasets

questions.modelAnswer: Big-O notation describes the upper bound of how an algorithm scales in time or memory as input size increases. It ignores constant factors and minor terms to focus on long-term growth. Interviewers use it to verify that candidate code will run efficiently on large datasets without slowing down the device.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between time complexity and space complexity? Answer in 2–4 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Defines time complexity as measuring the number of operations or execution steps
Defines space complexity as measuring extra memory allocated during execution
Notes that space complexity includes auxiliary data structures and recursive call stack frames

questions.modelAnswer: Time complexity measures how the number of operations grows as input size increases. Space complexity measures the extra memory an algorithm allocates during execution. This space includes new collections like arrays or dictionaries, as well as call stack frames used during recursion.

questions.prompt: Why is string.isEmpty faster than string.count == 0 in Swift? Explain the difference in time complexity. Answer in 2–4 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains string.isEmpty is O(1) constant time because it checks startIndex == endIndex
Explains string.count is O(n) linear time because Swift characters are extended grapheme clusters
Notes Swift must inspect Unicode scalar boundaries across the string to count characters

questions.modelAnswer: In Swift, string.isEmpty runs in O(1) constant time by checking if the start index equals the end index. In contrast, string.count takes O(n) linear time because Swift characters are extended grapheme clusters. Swift must inspect Unicode scalar boundaries across the whole string to count characters accurately.

questions.prompt: Why does calling array.contains inside a loop take O(n^2) time? How do you optimize it to O(n)? Answer in 2–4 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains array.contains takes O(n) linear time, causing an outer loop to multiply into O(n^2)
Explains converting the array to a Set allows O(1) average lookup time
States total optimized runtime becomes O(n) linear time

questions.modelAnswer: Calling array.contains inside a loop takes O(n^2) time because the outer loop runs n times and linear search takes O(n) time. To optimize this, convert the lookup array into a Set before the loop. Set lookups take O(1) average time, reducing the total runtime to O(n).

questions.prompt: Why does deep recursion consume memory even when a function allocates no local variables or arrays? How can this issue be prevented? Answer in 2–4 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains each recursive function call places a stack frame onto the system call stack
States recursion to depth n consumes O(n) stack memory, risking stack overflow
Explains rewriting the algorithm iteratively with a loop reduces auxiliary space to O(1)

questions.modelAnswer: Even without local variables, each recursive call pushes a stack frame onto the call stack. A recursion depth of n consumes O(n) stack memory, which can cause a stack overflow crash on large inputs. Rewriting the algorithm iteratively with a loop eliminates recursive frames and reduces space complexity to O(1).
